clue.text: Bore finished touring ancient city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for finished wraps round the city

parts.note: finished means ended
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A tedious person has finished a sightseeing trip round an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a noun for a dull person; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, and to bear hardship is to put up with or tolerate it.

clue.text: Once vigorous son is certainly not inspiring

parts.note: ex means former, once
hale means healthy and vigorous
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A formerly energetic son is now thoroughly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' is taken literally as breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out is the opposite of breathing in, the literal sense of inspiration.

clue.text: Reserved account, one not in my own branch?

definitions.text: one not in my own branch?

parts.note: distant means aloof or reserved
a relation is a telling or account of events

explanation.surface: A standoffish bank statement from someone working at another branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch' suggests a bank; it is a branch of a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote kinsman belongs to another branch of the family tree rather than one's own line.

clue.text: Danish ore, possibly coming from former colony

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Mineral ore from Denmark may actually have come from an old colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former British colony now Zimbabwe, and this adjective means native to it.

clue.text: Fundamental belief in Humberside is minimal

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: A core faith barely exists in the Humberside region of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Humberside is a former county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator God based on reason, a basic or minimal theism.

clue.text: Associate's in games area, back burning waste

indicators.note: in places the word for associate within the reversed games area
back tells us to read the games area word from right to left

parts.note: a rec (recreation ground) is a British playing field
to associate is to link; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A colleague is on the playing field, with something smouldering in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning waste' reads as an action but names the residue; 'back' and 'in' both act on the games area, read as CER.
explanation.definitionFit: The stony residue left in a furnace after coal is burned is called this, a kind of slag.

clue.text: Maxim for holding one's own hand tool?

parts.note: coping means managing, holding one's own
a saw is an old saying or maxim

explanation.surface: A proverb about keeping your own hand to yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying and the managing combine as a coping saw, for 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coping saw is a small handsaw with a thin blade for cutting curves.

clue.text: Utopia's international trade

definitions.note: read as Utopia is, a perfect imagined state

parts.note: a deal is a trade or bargain

explanation.surface: A perfect world is one with free global commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is a perfect society, the model or perfection of what one aspires to.

clue.text: Calm down and don't put too much money on that horse!

definitions.meaning: an idiom telling someone not to lose their temper

definitions.text: don't put too much money on that horse!
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a warning not to gamble even your clothing on a bet

explanation.surface: A friend urges you to relax and not bet heavily on a nag.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to stay calm; literally it warns against losing the clothes off one's back.

clue.text: Boundless trees chopped by weary pensioner

indicators.note: chopped by means cut into, so the weary word splits the trimmed trees
boundless means without its edges, so the outer letters of trees go

parts.note: to tire is to weary

explanation.surface: A pensioner, too tired to go on, fells trees without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundless' strips the first and last letters of trees, and 'chopped by' means the weary word cuts into what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has stopped working and draws a pension is one who has retired from work.

clue.text: Inept choristers horribly tense

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Incompetent choir members sing so badly that everyone is on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective meaning nervous; it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, this is the use of present-time verbs to narrate past events for vividness.

clue.text: Don't take holiday

definitions.meaning: to not take it with you

explanation.surface: Advice not to use up your vacation days.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: leave as a verb means abandon or not take, and as a noun means permitted absence from work.

clue.text: Drunken men docked in early naval vessel

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering, so the letters reel into a new order
docked means cut short, so the last letter of men goes

parts.note: taken as written before docking

explanation.surface: Sailors came aboard drunk in the early hours, the ship having docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks nautical but cuts MEN to ME; ME, IN and EARLY are then shuffled by 'Drunken'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a warship designed to lay explosive mines at sea.

clue.text: Men on TV co-ordinated manoeuvres

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the television word comes beside the men word

parts.note: a TV set
chessmen are pieces

explanation.surface: Television performers carry out rehearsed movements in sync.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, rehearsed routines from a free kick or corner are called this; also planned set routines generally.

clue.text: King, say, to go out with queen in rascal's clutches

parts.note: to court is to date or go out with

indicators.note: in, with clutches, means held inside the rascal
clutches means grip, so the queen is gripped by the rascal word

parts.note: a cad is a rascal or bounder
R is Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A king dates a queen who is held by a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks royal but is a playing card; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are the picture cards in a pack, an example.

clue.text: Car from Triumph, last of range

parts.note: a coup is a notable success or triumph

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of range

explanation.surface: A vehicle from the Triumph company, the final model in its line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triumph' looks like the British car maker; it is a victory, COUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupe is a two-door motor body style with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Sauce ingredient regularly ran, if stored in shade

indicators.note: stored in means placed inside the shade word

parts.note: a shade is a colour

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of ran if

explanation.surface: A recipe where a sauce component regularly runs, if kept in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflour is a starch used to thicken sauces, so a sauce component.

clue.text: Pick up fish, placing first two at the rear

indicators.text: placing first two at the rear
indicators.note: says the opening pair of letters move to the end of the word for fish

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Instructions for catching fish, with the first two moved to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, as gleaners collect leftover grain or facts.

clue.text: Rocks acceptable as shelter for black oryx

indicators.note: as shelter for means the rocks and acceptable words together enclose the black letter

parts.note: rocks is slang for gems
OK means acceptable
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Boulders make decent cover for a dark-coloured antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The gemsbok is a large southern African antelope, a species of oryx.

clue.text: Appearing for trial, blocks all but last over

parts.note: to be up before a court is to appear for trial

indicators.note: all but last means the final letter of the word for blocks is dropped

parts.note: wards off means fends off or blocks

explanation.surface: A defendant in court blocks every attempt bar the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means more than, as in a figure exceeding some amount.

clue.text: Bush in garden providing very early cover?

definitions.text: Bush in garden providing very early cover?

parts.words: Bush in garden providing very early cover?
parts.note: Eden's garden: Adam and Eve covered themselves with its leaves, the first clothing

explanation.surface: A shrub in the garden that sprouts its foliage early in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden is Eden; in Genesis, Adam and Eve sewed its leaves into the first garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Its leaves were the first clothing in Genesis, cover at the very start of history.

clue.text: Carnivore satisfied having consumed a meal? I'm not sure

indicators.note: having consumed means the word for satisfied takes in the meal

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it, so met
tea is an evening meal in Britain
er is a hesitant sound expressing doubt

explanation.surface: A meat-lover, full after a meal, hesitates over whether that really counted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having consumed' puts the article and the meal inside the satisfied word, giving MEATEAT; tea is the British evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnivore is an animal or person whose diet is flesh, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Playwright leaving behind western ridge

indicators.note: leaving behind means the playwright drops the letter for western

parts.note: Arnold Wesker was a British playwright (Chips with Everything)

explanation.surface: A dramatist turns his back on the West and heads for the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: An esker is a long winding ridge of gravel left by a glacial meltwater stream.

clue.text: Caesar's last day in Rome goes on

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the word Caesar

parts.note: the Ides was a fixed day in the Roman calendar, famously Caesar's death day

explanation.surface: Caesar's final day in Rome continues, the Ides of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes R from Caesar (the 's is a link); the Ides of March was when Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle, so goes on, in that sense.

clue.text: I must quit office job, being shy

indicators.note: must quit says the letter I leaves the word for office job

parts.note: filing is a routine clerical task

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to leave an office post because they are timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like bashful but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw something, as at a coconut shy; to fling is likewise to hurl.

clue.text: Conventionally-run snack bar torrid storm ultimately demolished

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are rebuilt in another order
ultimately picks the last letter of storm

explanation.surface: A sweltering roadside café is wrecked by a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes traditional businesses with physical shops rather than online trade, i.e. run in the customary way.

clue.text: Family type with left-wing tendencies

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
red describes a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A household whose members lean politically to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives, collectively a family.

clue.text: Yankee enthralled by singer playing instrument

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive within, so the letter sits inside
playing suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American is captivated by a vocalist performing on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks musical but rearranges SINGER; Y then goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe is a medical instrument for injecting or drawing fluid; also the panpipe of Greek myth.
